scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The One-Step emerged in the United States around 1910, reaching a peak in popularity by 1914 before spreading internationally, particularly in France between 1925 and 1930.
It evolved directly from the Turkey Trot, stripping away controversial elements until only the basic walking step remained.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Served as a primary social dance for public gatherings, hotel teas, and ballroom exhibitions, symbolizing modern urban sophistication and shedding the crude connotations of its predecessor.
Today it is a historical tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Danced in a closed couple position, the One-Step consists of walking steps, pivots, and structured figures.
Key movements include the Turn, the Dip, the Grapevine, the One-Step Eight, and the Square figure.
The man leads all movements while the woman follows.
Watch for Castle Walk, The Turn, The Dip.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (w_le0Q5D5IE)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couples traveling counter-clockwise around the room

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Performed to ragtime music and early jazz bands, the One-Step is set to a 2/4 meter.
Early musical examples include James M. Gallatly's 'Bogey Walk' and the 'Original Dixieland One-Step' (1917).
Listen for the piano, early jazz band instruments.
The pulse is 2/4.
Bright 2/4 ragtime and early jazz accompaniment featuring syncopated piano rhythms and driving percussion designed to maintain a steady walking beat for dancers.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Mr. and Mrs. Vernon Castle (inventors and introducers of the Castle Walk), Troy Kinney (dance historian who documented its origins), and James M. Gallatly (composer).
Includes variations such as the Castle Walk, Flower Bonnet One-Step, Spanish One-Step, Judy Walk, Bunny Hug, and the adaptation of Tango figures like the Square.
Directly descended from the Turkey Trot; closely related to and sharing figures with the Foxtrot, Quickstep, Tango, Boston Waltz, and Brazilian Maxixe.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: One-Step is parent of Turkey Trot: The One-Step originated from the Turkey Trot, retaining only its basic step while removing controversial mannerisms.
One-Step is sibling of Foxtrot: Assimilated alongside the One-Step into ragtime-derived dance forms.
One-Step is influence of Tango: Contributed figures such as the Square to the One-Step repertoire.
